recipes.name: Summer Grilled Cabbage
ingredients_raw: 1 large head cabbage, cored and cut into 8 wedges
0.5 teaspoon garlic powder, or to taste
0.5 teaspoon seasoned salt, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.

Arrange cabbage wedges in the bottom of a large metal baking dish; add water to dish. Place 1 teaspoon butter onto each wedge; season liberally with garlic powder, seasoned salt, and black pepper. Cover the dish with aluminum foil.
Place the dish on the preheated grill; cook until cabbage is tender, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Summer Grilled Cabbage
raw_recipe.description: Summer grilled cabbage is seasoned with butter, garlic powder, seasoned salt, and black pepper. It's an easy, six-ingredient grilled summer side dish.

review.reviewBody: This was so good! I never thought of doing cabbage on the grill. It tasted like Haluski with out the noodles! I didn't bother with the whole metal baking dish thing. I just cut the cabbage into wedges and removed the core. I cut pieces of foil big enough for each wedge then sprayed the foil with Pam so nothing would stick. I seasoned each wedge with a bit of salt, pepper, and minced garlic. I put a bat of butter inside and wrapped them up. Delicious - I'll definitely make these again.

This is not something I would have thought of doing with cabbage but it was so good. Grilling it makes the cabbage sweet and the outer edges that caramelize on the grill are so good. Just be careful they don't burn. Like others, I did this in individual foil packets. Instead of doing wedges, I sliced the cabbage head straight through like cauliflower steaks and I think it grilled more evenly that way. I put seasoning, butter pats, and a few sprinkles of water on each before I wrapped up the packets and then grilled them for about 30 minutes. A really yummy, low carb veg addition to my grilling repertoire. You'll surprise everyone with how good these come out and best of all you don't have to stink up the house by cooking cabbage inside.

This is probably one of my FAVORITE summer sides. I cut the cabbage into quarters. Then I put 2 pieces of thick cut bacon on top of each with about 2 tablespoons of butter, lightly salt with garlic salt and pepper. Then I generously wrap each quarter individually in foil. That way guests can just take a wrapper and go. I leave mine on the grill for about 40 minutes but I am also opening the grill a lot flipping steaks, cooking corn etc. So make sure to take that into account as well. It’s melt in your mouth heaven! Enjoy!

I did this on my george foreman (being an apartment with no outside access dweller).

I then added it to my kelbasa, onions, and egg pasta. Stuck all in crockpot and I think the grilled versus sauted cabbage made a nice difference than usual.

I've been making cabbage "steaks" in the oven for years - slice full rounds, 1" thick - brush with olive oil - season liberally with salt, pepper & garlic powder & bake on a cookie sheet for 1/2 hour. Turn half way through to brown on both sides. The crispy outside pieces are the BEST!

My grandmother taught me this years ago. For a spicier version, season with cayenne pepper. I wrap individual wedges in foil. The moisture content cooks the cabbage. If you aren't up to lighting the grill, this works very well in a 450 degree oven...tightly covered heavy pan-no foil.

Good recipe! I wrapped my wedges in aluminum foil I sprayed with cooking spray and sprinkled them with salt, pepper and garlic powder (topped with the dab of butter). Perfect with some salty smoked sausages we grilled.

It turned out awesome! I cut cabbage wedges, used a tad of margarine, minced garlic, and red onion circles and wrapped it all in foil. Cooked on grill 25 minutes and added salt and pepper to taste before serving. Turned out wonderful

Isnt cabbage on the grill awesome! But I use just foil and wrap wedges indivuallly there is no mess and each serving can be customed if you have different tastes in the family like I do! That way you dont have to ruin a baking dish. Also reyonld wrap has the "foil bags" you can use if you are doing a large order!

This was very good. Even better than expected. I just wrapped the seasoned cabbage wedge in foil with the butter and put it on the grill. Very easy. I’ll make this again soon since I still have uncooked cabbage available.

O.K. If you are looking to impress some friends. Show up for their cook-out with these prewrapped in individual foil and put them on the grill away from the direct heat and watch the fun as the guest open their little packet of goodness. I have cooked this recipe many times. The only thing I add is a sliced onion as a last step.

I made this several times. I followed the recipe exactly the first time and it was good, but the second time... WOW! The only difference was that I used the seasonings that we like, and since I had eight pieces I seasoned two one way, two another etc. and we simply loved it.

Everyone should realize there are concerns about the use of aluminum foil. Using it to seal in moisture on a metal baking dish is fine. Wrapping food directly in foil and cooking it is concerning. I was reading this recipes reviews and people said over and over they were sealing the cabbage in foil. There are worse things that cleaning a steel baking pan.

This was an awful mushy mess! 30 minutes is waaay to long. And, I can’t believe I’m going to say this but IMHO this is the one vegetable that should not be grilled. Although Hubby liked the flavor, so I humored him by trying it again, but cooking it for about 10 minutes. 10 minutes is still too long for w, bcuz I like crunchy veggies. But, the smokiness for cabbage is not my thing.
This is great, I added bacon to the top but that was my only variation.
Delicious - I used a couple types of “seasoning salt” but will use only Lawry’s seasoning salt in the future - it was by far the best.
Simple and delicious. Also, it makes a great coleslaw.

Ive been doing this for years. I too use foil packets. I cut the cabbage in smaller pieces, just a personal preference. I change it up frequently using ranch or Italian dressing seasoning mix or corn on the cob chipotle seasoning for a little kick. Love love love cabbage on the grill! I do it in the oven in the winter, not quite the same but sometimes I just need my cabbage fix.
First of all, if it’s metal, it’s a sheet, not a dish. Second, if you’re grilling the cabbage on a baking sheet, why are you oiling the grill. A little confused...
This was a hit. Instead of cutting the cabbage into wedges I just chopped it up and put it into a grill pan. Kept all other ingredients the same. Nice addition to grilled chicken and green beans.
